selection: Two smallest snippets, distinct institutions; convenience sample, not representative cohort
attribution: Kolbinger et al., Appendix300, Scientific Data (2026), DOI 10.1038/s41597-026-07593-6; dataset DOI 10.25532/OPARA-1173; CC BY 4.0

inspection.method: Sequential sampled frames inspected directly, plus simulator frame at 3 seconds; not full temporal tracking or segmentation
observations: Real frames contain fine branching vessels, lobulated yellow fat, thin membrane-like surfaces and overlapping tissue folds.
Specular highlights vary sharply with location and camera position; not uniform glossy pink shading.
Center1 sequence shows an instrument near tissue with changing occlusion and tissue configuration. Sampled frames do not establish quantitative force or deformation.
Center2 has an oval active image and wide stored frame; do not infer camera intrinsics from container aspect ratio.
Current simulator frame is dominated by smooth homogeneous surfaces and lacks comparable layered detail.
limitations: Convenience sample from two centers; not representative or held-out evaluation.
Downloaded durations are shorter than nominal 100-second snippets; do not assume all files share duration.
No force labels, calibrated camera, appendix segmentation, or 3D reconstruction inferred.
implementation_priorities: Replace generic smooth organ layout with appendix-cecum-mesoappendix context grounded in surgical views.
Model visible tissue layers and spatially varying surface appearance; avoid baking reference-image lighting into albedo.
Render integrated bimanual grasp and traction with local deformation and moving occlusion.
Compare actual rendered sequences against references before making visual-fidelity claims.
